---
description: File friction with a fathom tool the moment you hit it — symptom/tool/expected/actual/repro — via `fathom observe`, so it never dies unrecorded.
argument-hint: [TOOL=<tool-name>] [SYMPTOM="<what went wrong>"]
---

<!-- fathom:owned — generated by `fathom init --skills`; safe to delete this line to adopt the file as your own -->

> **Capability note.** `fathom observe` is a plain CLI verb — fully
> harness-agnostic, nothing Codex-specific here. This file just carries the
> convention into Codex CLI's custom-prompts mechanism
> (`~/.codex/prompts/fathom-feedback.md`, invoked as
> `/prompts:fathom-feedback`). If your Codex CLI has adopted the native
> `SKILL.md`-based skills mechanism (`.agents/skills/`), prefer copying this
> skill's `SKILL.md` there instead.

The moment a fathom tool gives a wrong answer, misses something you know is
there, has a confusing contract, or is slow/flaky — file it immediately,
before the task moves on:

```sh
fathom observe --symptom "$SYMPTOM" --tool "$TOOL" \
  --expected "<what should have happened>" \
  --actual "<what happened instead>" \
  --repro "<the exact call + response that reproduces it>"
```

This appends a structured entry to `.fathom/observations.md`: **symptom →
evidence (real reproduction) → root cause → fix → status** — the same shape
fathom's own team uses. `fathom instrument --adoption` surfaces the
open-observation count.

Never diagnose from a vague complaint — probe a known-good case alongside
the failing one so the entry actually root-causes the difference, not just
records a feeling that something was off.
